correctness.rationale: A beta integral proves the axial norm formula and an exact generating-function identity proves the polynomial numerator. Rational Cayley transforms and Routh arrays with no singular pivots and exact polynomial gcd exclusion of imaginary-axis roots give 0 interior zeros for m=1..8 and 2 for m=9. Positive coefficients of the original kernel on (0,1), alternating Q_m coefficients on (-1,0), and conjugation imply the two m=9 roots are nonreal simple. The standalone verify.py recalculates all required exact rational certificates; numeric locations are illustrative.

value.rationale: The first geometrically natural complex-dimension threshold at which equal quartic-core cylinder intersections acquire central-axis Bergman zeros is a concrete Lu Qi-Keng obstruction. The sharp first-fibre threshold and rigid two-root count, not the known general kernel series, are mathematically motivated and materially stronger than isolated sample calculations; they furnish a reproducible benchmark for higher-dimensional cylinder kernels. The scope is deliberately limited to the axial census through m=9.
